assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational framework connecting collateral constraints to macroeconomic fluctuations and financial crises, with exceptional influence across theory and policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied the central collateral-cycle mechanism; Gertler made closely related financial-accelerator mechanisms central to modern macroeconomics.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has been extensively developed, tested, and incorporated into macro-financial models over several decades.
uncertainties: The listed contribution encompasses related mechanisms with a broader set of important contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation program gave a tractable quantitative account of large productivity and income differences and redirected research toward firm-level distortions.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Restuccia, and Klenow are strongly associated with the central measurement and quantitative framework.
assessment.maturity: It is a mature and widely used research program, with an extensive subsequent literature applying and refining it.
uncertainties: Inference from dispersion measures to distortions and aggregate productivity remains debated.
The appropriate division of credit among the broader misallocation literature is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work substantially changed understanding of how trade and technology reshape local labour markets, employment, and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a coherent core for the influential empirical analysis of trade-exposure effects; Katz is also central to related task and wage-inequality research.
assessment.maturity: The findings have generated a large literature, enduring methodological debate, and major policy relevance.
uncertainties: Estimated local effects and their aggregation to national welfare remain sensitive to empirical design and adjustment horizons.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern New Keynesian framework provided a durable, policy-relevant synthesis of nominal rigidities, expectations, and monetary stabilization.
assessment.attribution: Calvo's pricing mechanism and Woodford's and Gali's framework-building work are central, though the contribution depends on many listed and unlisted contributors.
assessment.maturity: The framework has dominated academic and central-bank monetary analysis for decades.
uncertainties: The scope is unusually broad and makes a three-person attribution necessarily incomplete.
The empirical adequacy of core nominal-rigidity assumptions remains contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The management-practices research program established organizational capability as a measurable and consequential source of productivity differences.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen developed the central measurement agenda, with Sadun an important contributor to its organizational and policy extensions.
assessment.maturity: The program has been replicated internationally and has influenced both research and management policy.
uncertainties: Separating the causal effects of management practices from selection and complementary inputs remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade theory and empirical work on the distributional and productivity effects of globalization.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the indispensable originator of the canonical model, while Helpman and Redding made major complementary contributions to the broader program.
assessment.maturity: The framework is deeply embedded in trade research and has supported extensive empirical and quantitative applications.
uncertainties: Credit is difficult to delimit because the approach builds on earlier heterogeneous-firm and trade traditions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The reconstruction of long-run top-income and wealth distributions made inequality central to empirical economics and public-policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are central to the top-income series and their interpretation; Zucman made pivotal contributions on wealth and offshore holdings.
assessment.maturity: The underlying data work and resulting research program have persisted for many years and shaped a large international literature.
uncertainties: Capitalization, tax-record coverage, and offshore-wealth estimates involve consequential measurement choices.
The discovery is partly a data-building and synthesis achievement rather than a single unified theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and linked place-based conditions to life outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are core architects of the mobility research program, with Friedman an important collaborator in its administrative-data implementation.
assessment.maturity: The work has already generated broad replication, methodological development, and substantial policy relevance.
uncertainties: The causal interpretation of place effects and policy prescriptions remains an active research question.
The comparatively recent expansion of the literature warrants caution about ultimate maturity.
